import json, numpy as np, pandas as pd
import statsmodels.formula.api as smf
import statsmodels.api as sm
from pathlib import Path
from scipy import stats

# Load per-clause summary
df = pd.read_csv('artifacts/full_study/analysis/per_clause_summary.csv')
df['violation'] = df['violation_rate'].astype(float)
print(f'Loaded {len(df)} rows')

# Load clause templates for info delta (token count diff)
with open('artifacts/_project/data/clause_templates_full.json') as f:
    clauses = json.load(f)

# Build per-clause info delta: |tokens(unambiguous) - tokens(ambiguous)|
clause_info = {}
for c in clauses:
    cid = c['clause_id']
    amb = c.get('ambiguous_clause', '')
    unamb = c.get('unambiguous_clause', '')
    amb_tokens = len(amb.split())
    unamb_tokens = len(unamb.split())
    delta = unamb_tokens - amb_tokens  # positive = unambiguous is longer
    clause_info[cid] = {
        'amb_tokens': amb_tokens,
        'unamb_tokens': unamb_tokens,
        'info_delta': delta,
        'ambiguity_type': c.get('ambiguity_type', ''),
    }

# Merge info_delta into df
df['info_delta'] = df['clause_id'].map(lambda x: clause_info.get(x, {}).get('info_delta', 0))

# Add layer variable
ling_types = ['scopal', 'lexical', 'coreferential']
spec_types = ['incompleteness', 'conditional_precedence', 'authorization_scope']
df['layer'] = df['ambiguity_type'].apply(lambda x: 'specification' if x in spec_types else 'linguistic')

print(f'Info delta range: {df.info_delta.min()} to {df.info_delta.max()}, mean={df.info_delta.mean():.1f}')

# ===== Per-type info delta distribution =====
print('\n=== Per-type info delta ===')
per_type_delta = {}
for atype in sorted(df['ambiguity_type'].unique()):
    sub = df[df['ambiguity_type'] == atype]['info_delta']
    vals = sub.unique()  # same for all models, get unique per clause
    clause_deltas = df[df['ambiguity_type'] == atype].groupby('clause_id')['info_delta'].first()
    m, s = clause_deltas.mean(), clause_deltas.std()
    per_type_delta[atype] = {'mean': round(m, 2), 'sd': round(s, 2), 'n_clauses': len(clause_deltas)}
    print(f'  {atype}: {m:.1f} ± {s:.1f} (n={len(clause_deltas)})')

# ===== Model 1: violation ~ condition + ambiguity_type (baseline) =====
print('\n=== Model 1: baseline ===')
m1 = smf.logit('violation ~ C(condition) + C(ambiguity_type)', data=df).fit(disp=0)
print(m1.summary().tables[1])

# ===== Model 2: violation ~ condition + ambiguity_type + info_delta =====
print('\n=== Model 2: + info_delta ===')
m2 = smf.logit('violation ~ C(condition) + C(ambiguity_type) + info_delta', data=df).fit(disp=0)
print(m2.summary().tables[1])

# ===== Model 3: violation ~ condition + layer (to test layer effect) =====
print('\n=== Model 3: condition + layer ===')
m3 = smf.logit('violation ~ C(condition) + C(layer)', data=df).fit(disp=0)
print(m3.summary().tables[1])

# ===== Model 4: violation ~ condition + layer + info_delta =====
print('\n=== Model 4: condition + layer + info_delta ===')
m4 = smf.logit('violation ~ C(condition) + C(layer) + info_delta', data=df).fit(disp=0)
print(m4.summary().tables[1])

# ===== Compute coefficient changes =====
# Layer effect
layer_coef_m3 = float(m3.params['C(layer)[T.specification]'])
layer_p_m3 = float(m3.pvalues['C(layer)[T.specification]'])
layer_coef_m4 = float(m4.params['C(layer)[T.specification]'])
layer_p_m4 = float(m4.pvalues['C(layer)[T.specification]'])
layer_change_pct = abs(layer_coef_m4 - layer_coef_m3) / abs(layer_coef_m3) * 100

print(f'\n=== Layer effect change ===')
print(f'  Without info_delta: coef={layer_coef_m3:.4f}, p={layer_p_m3:.6f}')
print(f'  With info_delta:    coef={layer_coef_m4:.4f}, p={layer_p_m4:.6f}')
print(f'  Change: {layer_change_pct:.1f}%')

# Info delta in model 4
delta_coef_m4 = float(m4.params['info_delta'])
delta_p_m4 = float(m4.pvalues['info_delta'])
print(f'  Info delta coef: {delta_coef_m4:.6f}, p={delta_p_m4:.6f}')

# Check ambiguity_type coefficients change between m1 and m2
print(f'\n=== Type coefficients change (M1 vs M2) ===')
type_coef_changes = {}
for param in m1.params.index:
    if 'ambiguity_type' in param:
        c1 = float(m1.params[param])
        p1 = float(m1.pvalues[param])
        c2 = float(m2.params[param]) if param in m2.params.index else None
        p2 = float(m2.pvalues[param]) if param in m2.pvalues.index else None
        if c2 is not None and c1 != 0:
            change = abs(c2 - c1) / abs(c1) * 100
        else:
            change = None
        type_name = param.replace('C(ambiguity_type)[T.', '').rstrip(']')
        type_coef_changes[type_name] = {
            'coef_without_delta': round(c1, 4),
            'p_without_delta': round(p1, 6),
            'coef_with_delta': round(c2, 4) if c2 else None,
            'p_with_delta': round(p2, 6) if p2 else None,
            'change_pct': round(change, 1) if change else None
        }
        print(f'  {type_name}: {c1:.4f} (p={p1:.4f}) -> {c2:.4f} (p={p2:.4f}), change={change:.1f}%' if c2 else f'  {type_name}: missing in m2')

# LR test: m1 vs m2
lr_stat = 2 * (m2.llf - m1.llf)
lr_p = 1 - stats.chi2.cdf(lr_stat, df=1)
print(f'\n  LR test (m1 vs m2): chi2={lr_stat:.4f}, p={lr_p:.6f}')

# LR test: m3 vs m4
lr_stat_layer = 2 * (m4.llf - m3.llf)
lr_p_layer = 1 - stats.chi2.cdf(lr_stat_layer, df=1)
print(f'  LR test (m3 vs m4): chi2={lr_stat_layer:.4f}, p={lr_p_layer:.6f}')

# ===== Correlation between info_delta and ambiguity_type =====
# VIF proxy: correlation
clause_level = df.groupby('clause_id').first()
corr_delta_type = clause_level.groupby('ambiguity_type')['info_delta'].mean()
print(f'\nPer-type mean info_delta: {dict(corr_delta_type.round(1))}')

# ===== Build output =====
output = {
    'analysis_name': 'Per-Clause Info Delta Covariate Analysis',
    'motivation': 'Response to reviewer N3 (incompleteness confound) and MF-2 (info delta confound). Tests whether controlling for per-clause token delta changes type/layer effects.',
    'n_observations': len(df),
    'n_clauses': int(df['clause_id'].nunique()),
    'per_type_info_delta': per_type_delta,
    'models': {
        'model1_baseline': {
            'formula': 'violation ~ C(condition) + C(ambiguity_type)',
            'aic': round(float(m1.aic), 2),
            'bic': round(float(m1.bic), 2),
            'pseudo_r2': round(float(m1.prsquared), 4),
            'llf': round(float(m1.llf), 2)
        },
        'model2_with_info_delta': {
            'formula': 'violation ~ C(condition) + C(ambiguity_type) + info_delta',
            'aic': round(float(m2.aic), 2),
            'bic': round(float(m2.bic), 2),
            'pseudo_r2': round(float(m2.prsquared), 4),
            'llf': round(float(m2.llf), 2),
            'info_delta_coef': round(float(m2.params['info_delta']), 6),
            'info_delta_p': float(m2.pvalues['info_delta']),
            'info_delta_or': round(np.exp(float(m2.params['info_delta'])), 4)
        },
        'model3_layer_only': {
            'formula': 'violation ~ C(condition) + C(layer)',
            'layer_coef': round(layer_coef_m3, 4),
            'layer_p': layer_p_m3,
            'layer_or': round(np.exp(layer_coef_m3), 4),
            'aic': round(float(m3.aic), 2)
        },
        'model4_layer_with_info_delta': {
            'formula': 'violation ~ C(condition) + C(layer) + info_delta',
            'layer_coef': round(layer_coef_m4, 4),
            'layer_p': layer_p_m4,
            'layer_or': round(np.exp(layer_coef_m4), 4),
            'info_delta_coef': round(delta_coef_m4, 6),
            'info_delta_p': delta_p_m4,

        }
    },

tool_args.old_string: \citet{berry_kamsties_2004} distinguish nocuous from innocuous ambiguity based on whether stakeholders diverge on interpretation. Our results extend this framework to LLM agents: all six ambiguity types are nocuous ($+34.0$ pp overall), but both the type and the model determine severity. We propose \emph{Differential Nocuity} as an empirical regularity: the risk of a policy ambiguity is not an intrinsic property of the clause but a function of the ambiguity type, the agent's safety training, and the availability of external disambiguation channels. The dominance of clause identity over model identity (22:1 variance ratio) grounds this universality empirically. Moreover, 41.3\% of ambiguous clauses trigger majority-convergent violations---a pattern we term \emph{systematic nocuity}, where all models converge on the same wrong interpretation. If models violated independently at the observed 41\% base rate, the probability of $\geq 3/5$ convergence would be ${\sim}23\%$; the observed 41.3\% indicates correlated failure driven by shared pretraining biases, making the error invisible in inter-model agreement metrics.
